description: Twin-store probes must use the explicit path to OUR binary (/home/denkhaus/dev/mulch/target/debug/mulch), never a bare 'mulch' from PATH: the npm package @os-eco/mulch-cli 0.10.7 installs its own 'mulch' shim on PATH (same name, the reference JS implementation) — a probe round that shells out to 'mulch' compares the reference with itself and silently 'passes'. Caught by the sprint-26 spec reviewer.
resolution: Ad-hoc probe snippets pin the explicit debug path (or CARGO_BIN_EXE_mulch); the battery helpers are already explicit. The trap is the misnamed bare command, not the probe design.

name: parallel-writer-tests-need-unique-dedup-keys
description: Parallel-writer CLI tests (writer-lock class) must give every concurrent writer a UNIQUE dedup key (distinct --name AND --content for conventions — the dedup key is type+content-family). First draft raced 8 records with identical --content: all 8 processes succeeded, but the store held ONE record — correct upsert/dedup semantics, wrong test. The "lost records" assertion then fires for the wrong reason and points at the lock, not the fixture. Same discipline as time-dependent fixtures: assert on a store shape the command cannot legitimately collapse.
